source.title: Check If a String Contains All Binary Codes of Size K

teaching.hint: How many different required strings are there, and how much information must describe one fixed-length candidate?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Exactly 2^k codes are required, and each length-k binary window has an exact k-bit integer representation.
solution_outline.approach: Reject if there are fewer windows than required codes. Otherwise scan the binary windows using an exact shifting-and-masking representation, mark observed codes, and accept once every code has appeared.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The maintained low k bits encode the current full window, including leading zeroes; the marked set contains exactly the codes seen at processed starts.
solution_outline.correctness: Appending a bit and dropping the oldest one gives precisely the next window’s integer code. The representation bijects the length-k strings with integers below 2^k, so distinct marked codes equal distinct observed strings. All required strings occur exactly when all codes are marked; too few windows cannot cover them.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n+2^k)` time and `O(2^k)` auxiliary space; after the window-count guard, allocated inputs have 2^k<=n, so time is `O(n)`.
solution_outline.pitfall: Do not mark a partially filled window or forget leading zeroes; if k exceeds string length there are no full windows.

source_fidelity_notes: Clarified fixed-length codes with leading zeroes and overlapping substrings; retained full n/k bounds.
common_wrong_turns: Do not mark a partially filled window or forget leading zeroes; if k exceeds string length there are no full windows.
